sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a determinant as a 'scaling factor' for area/volume during a linear transformation. Prerequisite: Students should know that a matrix represents a transformation of space.
sections.example: Imagine a 2D square representing a territory of a cat. When the matrix transformation is applied, the square becomes a parallelogram. The determinant is the ratio of the new area to the original area.

sections.title: Defining the 2x2 Determinant
sections.content: Define the determinant for a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] as ad - bc. Use a visual animation showing the area of the parallelogram formed by vectors (a, c) and (b, d).
sections.example: For matrix [[2, 0], [0, 2]], the area is 2*2 - 0*0 = 4. Visualize the original square being stretched uniformly in both dimensions.

sections.title: Geometric Nuance: Orientation and Sign
sections.content: Explain that a negative determinant indicates that the orientation of space has been 'flipped' (like a mirror reflection).
sections.example: Visualize a clock face. A positive determinant keeps the hands moving clockwise; a negative determinant flips the face, making the hands move counter-clockwise.

sections.title: The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions
sections.content: Explain what happens when the determinant is zero. The transformation collapses the space into a line or a point, meaning information is lost.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D drone mapping a 3D room. If the determinant of its transformation matrix is 0, the drone 'flattens' the 3D room into a 2D plane, losing the depth data entirely.

sections.title: Summary and Connection
sections.content: Recap: Determinant = Scaling Factor. Positive = Same orientation, Negative = Flipped orientation, Zero = Dimensional collapse.
sections.example: A quick animation showing a 3x3 cube squashing into a flat plate (det=0) vs expanding to a larger cube (det>1) or shrinking (0 < det < 1).

storyboard.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: Matrices represent a transformation of space.
Think of space as a cat's territory.
Transformations stretch, rotate, or shear space.
The determinant acts as a scaling factor.
It measures how area changes after transformation.
animations: Display 2x2 grid representing unit square with color #FF00FF.
Show grid scaling by factor 2 with color #FFFF00.
Visualize area expanding from 1 to 4 units.
Highlight scaling transformation matrix with color #00FFFF.
Emphasize final area result with color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Defining the 2x2 Determinant
lecture_lines: Area is defined by ad minus bc.
animations: Display matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] with color #FFFFFF.
Highlight elements a and d with color #00FF00.
Highlight elements b and c with color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Geometric Nuance: Orientation and Sign
lecture_lines: Think of it like a mirror reflection.
animations: Show unit square with orientation color #0000FF.
Rotate square to show sign flip with color #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions
lecture_lines: Dimensions are lost in the process.
animations: Show 2D space transforming into a single line.
Fade lines to color #808080 showing collapse.
Place zero in middle with color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Summary and Connection
lecture_lines: Determinant is the transformation scaling factor.
Sign tells us about space orientation.
Zero means the space has collapsed.
